chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah from Sulayman ibn Hashim from Salim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Four mosques were renovated in Kufa as a celebration for the killing of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) — the mosque of al-Ash'ath, the mosque of Jarir, the mosque of Simak, and the mosque of Shabath ibn Rabi'iy — may Allah curse them.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali, the third Imam.
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Kufa, a major city in Iraq and a significant center of early Shia history.
key_terms.فَرَحاً: As a celebration or joy, indicating the emotional context of the action.
key_terms.لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ: May Allah curse them, a formula of divine condemnation against the individuals mentioned.
key_terms.لِقَتْلِ: For the killing/martyrdom, referring specifically to the event of Imam Husayn.

ai.seo_question: Which four mosques in Kufa were renovated to celebrate the killing of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the political and religious symbolism of architecture in early Kufa, where four prominent mosques were renovated as acts of gratitude for the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (AS). The specific mention of the owners—Al-Ash'ath, Jarir, Simak, and Shabath—underscores their role in the Umayyad-aligned faction, linking their architectural patronage to the theological concept of *al-wala' wa al-barra'* (alliance and enmacy). The concluding curse serves as a scholarly indicator of their spiritual standing relative to the Ahl al-Bayt.
